newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Interleisure details sales to Kersaf, MIH.
newsitem.headline: Interleisure details sales to Kersaf, MIH.

text.p: South African entertainment group Interleisure Ltd said on Wednesday it had sold its movie ticket business, Computicket, to Multichoice for 35 million rand.
At the same time Interleisure said it had sold a 70 percent stake in Ster-Kinekor Management (Jersey) Ltd to Kersaf Ltd for 22.4 million rand.

Details of these further sales follow the announcement on Tuesday that media group Primedia Ltd had bought the bulk of Interleisure's interests in a massive deal worth 1.5 billion rand. Primedia would finance the deal through a combination of cash, debt and the issue of Primedia units.

Kersaf had also been granted an option until August 31 to buy Interleisure's 20 percent stake in Broadcasting Development Services Ltd (BDS), to be operated as Station for the Nation, for 1.1 million rand. BDS is currently preparing an application for a television licence.
Multichoice, a subscriber television management service firm, trades as MIH Holdings Ltd on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

Interleisure said that subsequent to the disposals it will hold 263.4 million rand in cash, 35.9 million Primedia ordinary combined units, 15.4 million Primedia "N" combined units and 96.4 million shares in fellow media grouping Sasani Ltd, in which it holds a stake.

It is proposed that Interleisure will be unbundled and voluntarily liquidated so that shareholders will directly acquire an interest in Primedia and Sasani Ltd as well as a cash payment after liquidation costs.
Interleisure shareholders may also elect to receive a cash underpin of 25.50 rand per Primedia combined unit.
